sentences.text: Cryonectes was a moderate-sized pliosaurid with a skull measuring 47 cm in length. This predator featured a greatly elongated snout and a long lower jaw with a distinct ventral ridge.
The name Cryonectes translates to 'cold swimmer,' honoring the cool climate of its time. Its species name, neustriacus, honors the ancient Frank kingdom of Neustria in northwest France.

The fossil was collected in the 1980s from the Calcaire à Bélemnites Formation near Laize-la-Ville, south of Caen. Peggy Vincent, Nathalie Bardet, and Emanuela Mattioli formally named the genus in 2012, establishing Cryonectes neustriacus as the type species. The holotype consists of a partial skull, an articulated mandible, and ten associated vertebrae.
Evidence suggests the specimen was a subadult individual at a relatively early stage of development.
Cladistic analysis places Cryonectes as basal to Pliosaurus, Peloneustes, and other pliosaurids. It is classified within the family Pliosauridae.
Cryonectes lived during the Early Jurassic period, specifically the upper Pliensbachian stage. The time range for this animal is estimated between 192.9 and 184.2 million years ago.
